wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Iran, a country of roughly 90 million people whose oil exports, nuclear programme and confrontation with Washington make it one of the pages people open when the Gulf is in the news.
wiki-iran.recent: US forces struck three Iranian crude tankers and the IRGC said it hit six in reply, while blasts sounded near the Kharg Island export terminal. Iran's security chief vowed to declare a prohibited zone near the Strait of Hormuz, and Energy Secretary Chris Wright said there may be no nuclear agreement at all.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of light, sweet North Sea crude, and the benchmark most seaborne oil outside the Americas is sold against. Roughly three-quarters of the world's traded crude is priced off it, so refined-fuel costs follow it.
brent.recent: US forces struck three Iranian tankers and Iran said it hit six in reply, with blasts near the Kharg Island export terminal and a supertanker stopped by mines in the strait. Iran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone at Hormuz, and OPEC+ left quotas unchanged rather than covering an outage. US pump prices reached $4.03 a gallon.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of West Texas Intermediate, the light sweet crude pumped in the US shale basins and delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma. It is the contract American refiners and drillers price against, and it sets US pump prices.
wti.recent: US forces struck three Iranian crude tankers and Iran says it hit six in reply, with the IRGC warning vessels off Hormuz and Tehran vowing a prohibited zone; three tankers turned back rather than transit. OPEC+ met in Riyadh and left quotas untouched, declining to replace the barrels the war is blocking.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas delivered to a pipeline hub in Erath, Louisiana, where most American gas contracts settle. It sets what US power plants, factories and LNG exporters pay, and it decouples from European and Asian gas prices because pipelines, not ships, define its market.
natgas-hh.recent: US gas has stayed cheap while Europe scrambled: EU storage sits near 64% and the Dutch benchmark topped €75 per megawatt-hour, pulling spot LNG cargoes east. That competition landed abroad rather than at home — Delhi raised compressed natural gas by ₹3.89 a kg and Pakistan apologized for blackouts after a delayed RLNG cargo.

wheat.standing: The world price of a tonne of milling wheat, the grain that feeds more people directly than any other. Importing countries budget bread subsidies against it, and it is the crop whose price most reliably turns into political trouble.
wheat.recent: The UN's food price index rose for a third month to 133.3 points, driven by cereals, as extreme weather cut harvests across the northern hemisphere — France's maize harvest fell to a four-decade low after summer drought. Forecasters put the odds near 100% that a record-strength El Niño persists to February.

rice.standing: The world reference price for milled white rice, quoted by the IMF in dollars a tonne. Rice is the staple grain for more people than any other crop, and import bills across Asia and West Africa move with this number.
rice.recent: The UN food agency put its price index up a third straight month, to 133.3 points, on cereals and sugar, with conflict and extreme weather named as the drivers. That basket figure does not break rice out, and nothing else this month accounts for where this contract has gone.

copper.standing: The world price of refined copper, quoted per tonne. It is the metal that carries current, so demand for it rises with every kilometre of transmission line, every substation and every motor built.
copper.recent: The window's copper story is grid buildout and grid attack rather than mining supply: the White House barred foreign-made grid parts on maintenance grounds, Germany found homemade explosives at two substations and later along power lines in Saxony, and a Raleigh firm brought out a solid-state rival to the transformer. None of that fixes the price shown here.

us-10y.standing: The yield on the US government's benchmark 10-year note, set by what buyers will pay at auction and in the secondary market. It anchors mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs and the discount rate applied to assets worldwide.
us-10y.recent: The move came from the long end rather than policy: term premium widened as investors demanded more to hold duration, and Norway's sovereign wealth fund signalled it may cut $80bn of its Treasury holdings. An oil shock pushed odds of a Fed hike, not a cut, to two-in-three, and thirty-year yields touched a 2007 level.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted gauge of 500 large companies listed in the United States, chosen by a committee rather than by size alone. It is the benchmark most American retirement money is invested against.
sp500.recent: The window's backdrop was a bond market repricing: global yields reached multi-decade highs on inflation fears, and yields and the dollar rose again after a solid US jobs report on Sep 5, while the dollar had earlier fallen to its weakest since May on Waller's comments. None of that explains the index's path.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by market value. Software, chip and platform firms dominate it, so a handful of names set the direction for the whole index.
nasdaq100.recent: Nvidia agreed to pay $12.9 billion for Hugging Face, the neutral hub much of the open-model ecosystem is built on, folding a shared platform into a chip vendor's balance sheet. A judge in Alexandria ruled Google will not have to sell its ad exchange, leaving its advertising revenue intact. Apple handed the chief executive's job to John Ternus.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average pump price of a gallon of regular gasoline across US filling stations, surveyed weekly by the Energy Information Administration. It is the most visible price in American household budgets and follows crude oil and refining margins with a lag of days to weeks.
us-gas-retail.recent: The pump price passed $4.03 a gallon, above the 2012 peak, as the Iran war pushed crude through the Strait of Hormuz into every downstream fuel: US diesel set its own record at $5.85 a gallon, hitting California trucking and farms. The same war premium reached South African petrol, which rose R1.34 a litre despite a stronger rand.

natgas-ttf.standing: The Dutch Title Transfer Facility is where wholesale gas contracts are traded for delivery into the Netherlands, and the price the rest of Europe buys against. Industry and household heating bills follow it, and so do LNG cargoes.
natgas-ttf.recent: Europe went into the buying season with storage near 64%, well short of where the continent normally sits at that point, and had to bid against Asian buyers for the same spot LNG cargoes. The competition reaches beyond Europe: Delhi raised compressed natural gas by ₹3.89 a kg to ₹86.98, passing the cargo price through to drivers.

vix.standing: The Cboe Volatility Index, derived from S&P 500 option prices, measuring how much movement traders are paying to hedge against over the next 30 days. It rises when demand for protection rises, which is why it is read as a gauge of market stress.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar. Pakistan imports most of its fuel and much of its food, and buys both in dollars, so the rate sets the cost of living and the size of the external debt service bill.
fx-pkr.recent: Pakistan's external accounts drew support from the energy side: OGDCL booked a record Rs242.4bn profit, up 43%, and the power regulator moved to require batteries in an 800MW solar and wind auction that would cut imported-fuel generation. EU figures put Pakistan's 2024 tariff exemptions at €732 million, the export channel that earns the dollars.

fx-ngn.standing: The rate at which Nigeria's naira trades against the US dollar. Nigeria imports most refined fuel and much of its food, so the level of this rate feeds through to pump prices and inflation faster than to almost anything else.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira's firming came alongside foreign reserves hitting a 20-year high, which Moody's scored as a reward for austerity, and FTSE Russell's decision to reclassify Nigeria from Unclassified to frontier status on September 21 — a change that reopens index-tracking inflows. Working against it: Atiku Abubakar has pledged to restore the petrol subsidy in 2027.

fx-egp.standing: The Egyptian pound's exchange rate against the US dollar. Egypt imports most of its wheat and fuel and services heavy external debt in dollars, so the rate sets the price of bread, energy and repayment alike.
fx-egp.recent: A major Egyptian bank was cut off from the global financial system by the United States in late August, part of a push by Bessent against banks with Iran ties that also reached the UAE. Cairo spent the same fortnight courting alternatives, hosting Xi Jinping on his first state visit in a decade and pressing a Libya settlement.

fx-try.standing: The Turkish lira's exchange rate against the US dollar, quoted as lira per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker lira. Turkey imports most of its energy in dollars, and the rate sets the price of fuel and food for 85 million people.
fx-try.recent: The US Treasury sanctioned Golden Global Bank in Istanbul over Iran-linked dealings, putting a Turkish lender inside the American financial perimeter. Ankara also summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish ships in the Black Sea, and Erdogan pushed an SCO opening he insists is not a turn away from the West.

fx-bdt.standing: The Bangladeshi taka against the US dollar, quoted as taka per dollar. Bangladesh imports its fuel, food grain and industrial inputs in dollars and earns them back through garment exports and worker remittances, so the rate sets both the import bill and the value of money sent home.

fx-idr.standing: The rupiah's price against the US dollar. Indonesia is Southeast Asia's largest economy and a net exporter of coal, nickel and palm oil, so the currency tracks commodity earnings and the cost of the fuel and food the archipelago imports.
fx-idr.recent: Jakarta signed 138 oil and gas exploration blocks over to Russian bidders and pushed for early entry into force of its EAEU free trade agreement, with fertilizer and shipbuilding investment attached. Prabowo has meanwhile folded the cooperative system into his own economic apparatus.

fx-lbp.standing: The exchange rate of Lebanon's currency against the US dollar. After the banking collapse wiped out most of its value, the pound was refixed at a far weaker official rate, and salaries, subsidies and import prices in Lebanon are set against it.
fx-lbp.recent: Israeli strikes destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, killing seven, and the Lebanese health ministry counts 17 hospitals damaged since 2 March. Al Jazeera's carry puts the cumulative toll at nearly 9,000 killed since 2023. None of this explains the pound's movement, which stayed inside its managed band.

fx-cny.standing: The onshore price of one US dollar in Chinese yuan, the exchange rate the People's Bank of China guides within a daily band rather than letting it float. It sets the dollar cost of everything China exports.
fx-cny.recent: Beijing is pushing the currency outward through trade it already dominates: Shanghai's crude contract, settled in yuan, has gained enough price independence to be measured as a benchmark of its own, and US drugmakers now trace common antibiotics and blood thinners to Chinese suppliers. Xi used a Cairo platform to pitch Middle East states a security order without foreign bases.

fx-inr.standing: The exchange rate of India's rupee against the US dollar. It sets the dollar cost of the oil and gold India imports, the dollar value of remittances sent home, and the size India's economy appears to be in every table denominated in dollars.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee's path against the dollar is the reason India fell to sixth-largest economy while growing 7.8% in the June quarter: league tables convert nominal output at the market rate, so a weaker currency shrinks a country that is expanding. A separate revision cut last year's base by 7%, moving the ratio again without moving output.

fx-brl.standing: The exchange rate of Brazil's currency against the US dollar, quoted as reais per dollar. Brazil is a major exporter of soy, iron ore and oil, and the real is among the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies.
fx-brl.recent: Bank Master collapsed in a fraud probe that exposed how thinly Brazil's supervisors had been watching a mid-sized lender, leaving other banks of its size to be repriced on trust rather than balance sheets. A new poll showing the president's re-election lead evaporating added a second, political source of doubt about who sets fiscal policy next.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate of Mexico's peso against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends most of its exports north, so US trade policy and demand pass straight into the rate.

fx-eur.standing: The euro's exchange rate against the US dollar, quoted here as euros per dollar. It is the world's second most held reserve currency, and the price at which the trade of a 20-country monetary union is settled.
fx-eur.recent: Political ground shifted under the currency union's largest economy: Alternative for Germany took 44.5% in Saxony-Anhalt, its best result anywhere, and every other party's refusal to coalesce leaves a three- or four-way government to be assembled instead. Volkswagen said it would cut 50,000 more jobs worldwide.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate between Japan's currency and the US dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker yen. Japan imports almost all its fuel, and a cheap yen raises the cost of every barrel it lands.
fx-jpy.recent: The slide past 160 came from the gap between a Bank of Japan that has not moved and a Treasury market pricing thirty-year yields at 5.3%, a level last seen in 2007, with an oil shock pushing Fed hike odds to two-in-three. Treasury Secretary Bessent then pressed Tokyo publicly to raise rates.

fx-rub.standing: The number of rubles it takes to buy one US dollar, quoted by offshore data providers since Russia's currency stopped trading freely against the dollar in Western venues. It sets the ruble price of everything Russia imports, and the budget's oil revenue is booked in it.
fx-rub.recent: Ukrainian strikes reached the export infrastructure that earns the dollars: sea drones hit a vessel at Sochi and a strike set an oil depot ablaze more than 1,000km from the front. Novak's claim that 94% of oil now goes to 'friendly' countries describes a trade that clears at a discount, and households moved 4.2 trillion rubles into cash.

fx-zar.standing: The rand against the US dollar, Africa's most heavily traded currency and the one global investors use to take positions on the continent. It swings with metals prices and with foreign appetite for South African government debt.
fx-zar.recent: The currency's firmer level did not reach the pump: the fuel formula pushed petrol up R1.34 a litre from Tuesday, because the war premium and the levies in the price build-up are set separately from the exchange rate. Domestic fiscal strain kept pace — Gauteng's nurses gave the province a month over austerity in the health system.

btc.standing: The oldest and largest cryptocurrency, traded around the clock against every major currency. Its price is the sentiment gauge for the whole digital-asset market, and mining, exchanges and a growing set of listed treasury companies are levered to it.
btc.recent: The climb ran on a short squeeze and on "financial repression" trades ahead of Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole debut, with gold moving alongside it. Around it the plumbing strained: a bug in Liquid Network's Elements software drained roughly 4,000 bitcoin, and BlackRock cut its in-kind swap threshold from $25 million to $1 million.

eth.standing: The native token of the Ethereum network, used to pay for computation on the chain that hosts most lending protocols, stablecoins and token issuance. Its price is the closest thing to a valuation of that whole layer.
eth.recent: The rally ran alongside bitcoin's, which broke $80,000 on Aug 25 in a move CoinDesk desks tied to a $3 billion short squeeze and to positioning ahead of Warsh's Jackson Hole debut. Against that, Term Finance lost $8.5 million when an attacker bought enough governance votes to seize vault keys — a reminder that the applications built on the chain carry risks the token price does not.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by a London Good Delivery gold bar held in vaulted custody, so its price tracks bullion rather than crypto fundamentals. It gives crypto exchanges a way to trade the metal, and it moves with real interest rates and central-bank demand.
paxg.recent: A US payroll surge lifted bets on a September Federal Reserve hike, and higher policy rates weigh on a metal that pays no yield; that came days after Warsh's Jackson Hole speech, which traders had been pricing directly. Custody moved too: the Dutch central bank pulled $11.6bn of gold out of New York for London.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on artificial intelligence each day. It is a rough gauge of how far the subject has spread beyond the industry that builds it, rather than of anything the industry did.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Nvidia agreed to pay $12.9 billion for Hugging Face, the platform the open-model world had treated as neutral ground, and its founders were each left worth $1.8 billion. OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra to developers days later, and four AI services went down the same Thursday morning.

wiki-russia.standing: The English-language Wikipedia article on Russia, and a daily count of how many people open it. The number tracks how much of the world is looking up the country itself rather than any one story about it.
wiki-russia.recent: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner were sent to Moscow and Kyiv, and Zelenskyy ordered a battlefield halt for Sept. 5-8 to hold the talks, the first movement in frozen diplomacy. Around it, Ukrainian sea drones reached an oil depot near Sochi, over 1,000km from the front, and Germany closed Russia's consulate in Bonn after the failed Leipzig drone attack.

wiki-pakistan.standing: The daily count of people opening the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan, a country of some 250 million with a nuclear arsenal, a chronic balance-of-payments problem and contested borders with both India and Afghanistan.
wiki-pakistan.recent: The mid-August peak came as a fire in a hospital nursery in the capital killed 14 newborns. Attention held through late August, when army chief Asim Munir went to Tehran to revive Pakistan's mediation between Iran and the United States, then met Saudi and Turkish counterparts in Istanbul for the first committee session of the Mecca joint defence pact.

wiki-china.standing: The English Wikipedia article on China, and a daily count of how many people open it. It is a general reference page rather than a news page, so its readership is a rough gauge of how often the country is pulling people in from elsewhere.
wiki-china.recent: Xi Jinping went to Cairo for the first time in a decade and urged Middle East states to build a security order without foreign bases. Flash floods on August 26 near the Nepal-China border killed at least 95 people and shut the trade corridor; a Chinese worker was pulled from a tunnel ten days later.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman that links the Gulf to the Indian Ocean, and the only outlet for crude and LNG loaded at Gulf terminals. Its narrowest shipping lanes are a few kilometres wide, so a single closure reaches world energy prices.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: A supertanker hit mines in the strait on 31 August, and US drones later struck Iranian crude tankers under a tanker-for-tanker rule; three tankers turned back without a shot fired. Iran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone, and Trump floated renaming the waterway the Trump Strait.

wiki-india.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on India, a country of some 1.4 billion people whose economy, space programme and border disputes draw attention from far beyond South Asia.
wiki-india.recent: India grew 7.8% and still fell to sixth-largest economy, because the league table converts nominal output into dollars and a weaker rupee shrinks the measured total; a rebasing that cut last year's base by 7% drew further doubt about the figures. Modi met Putin and Xi at the SCO summit in Bishkek, and authorities demolished a mosque in Saharanpur.

wiki-ukraine.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine. It rises and falls with the war and the diplomacy around it, and works as a rough gauge of how much of the world is paying attention on any given day.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Ukraine ordered its forces to halt fighting from Sept. 5-8 to receive US envoys carrying a plan to end the war, after weeks in which the fighting instead widened: sea drones struck a vessel and an oil depot at Sochi, and Germany formally blamed Russia for a drone attack on Leipzig airport.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic thinned as the US and Iran traded strikes on shipping: Iran says it struck six tankers after US forces hit three, a supertanker was stopped after hitting mines, and three vessels turned back on a radio warning from the IRGC Navy without a shot fired. Iran's security chief vowed a new prohibited zone, and US diesel hit a record $5.85 a gallon.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthi forces pushed toward the strait from Mokha in early September, with 81 killed in a single day, while Yemen's army fought for the hills above Taiz at a cost of more than 120 lives since Thursday. A Houthi missile had already hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu, repricing war risk for the tankers that would otherwise transit here.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic still turns on the southern approach rather than on Egypt: Houthi forces attacked a vessel off Saudi Arabia and then advanced toward the strait at Mokha in fighting that killed 81, with Yemen's army claiming air strikes in Taiz. Cairo spent the same weeks on Xi Jinping's state visit and a Libya settlement push, neither of which touches the canal.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Two disruptions bracketed the strait's approaches. Anak Krakatau erupted at its southern end, closing Soekarno-Hatta and affecting 166,000 passengers, while smoke from Indonesian peat fires pushed Malaysia's king to declare a haze emergency in Sarawak. Meanwhile the US struck Iranian tankers and Iran struck back, unsettling the Hormuz crude that feeds this route.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic has run below its own baseline while the strait's politics sharpened: Taipei accused Beijing of espionage on the floor of the Pacific Islands Forum, and a US trade group pressed Washington to ban Chinese vehicles outright. The WMO says El Niño is near record strength with odds close to 100% it holds into February, which shapes the weather ships sail through here.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: The UN said in Geneva that odds are near 100% El Niño persists to February, with forecasters expecting the effect to run well into 2027 — the pattern that dries the Panama isthmus and drains the lake the locks spend on every ship. Rosatom is meanwhile pitching the Northern Sea Route as an alternative, targeting 100 million tonnes by 2032.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Two ships collided in the approaches off Silivri, sinking a Turkish cargo vessel and leaving 10 crew missing — the queue of ships waiting for a pilot and a transit slot is where the risk concentrates. Turkey also summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish-linked ships in the Black Sea, the trade the strait carries.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The strait's two shores spent the fortnight arguing about people rather than ships: more than 72,000 crossed into Ceuta in July, Morocco deported over 4,000 would-be crossers from Tangier in 20 days, and Spain's leader publicly questioned Moroccan border control as protests spread. Italy and Spain also extended Schengen checks to September 15.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Masked anti-migrant protesters blocked the roads into Dover on 5 September, shutting Britain's busiest ferry port and stalling cross-Channel freight; a council leader said police were slow to respond. Days earlier Macron and Burnham had met in London on border security, the issue the protest was staged against.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from the Gulf, not the southern route: US strikes on Iranian tankers near Kharg Island, an IRGC warning that turned three tankers back, and Iran vowing a prohibited zone in Hormuz. None of that reaches this passage, whose traffic follows whether the Red Sea is passable, not whether Hormuz is dangerous.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has stopped entirely. Ukrainian strikes have pushed deep into Russian waters and coastline — sea drones hit a vessel at Sochi and a strike set an oil depot burning nearby, over 1,000km from the front — leaving the Azov approaches too exposed for commercial sailing. Kyiv ordered a battlefield halt for Sept. 5-8 while US envoys travelled to Moscow and Kyiv.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The main index of the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh, tracking the listed companies on the Arab world's largest market by value, with Aramco the dominant weight. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: OPEC+ left its production quotas unchanged with Brent near $96, holding the oil revenue the index's largest constituent depends on. Riyadh also signed a joint defence pact with Pakistan and Turkey whose text is largely undisclosed, and shelled villages in Yemen's Razih district while Houthi forces claimed an attack on a vessel off the Saudi coast.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. Priced in lira, so its level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The US Treasury sanctioned Golden Global Bank over Iran-linked dealings, putting a listed Istanbul lender inside a compliance perimeter its peers have to price. Around it, Ankara summoned Kyiv's ambassador over strikes on Turkish ships in the Black Sea, and Erdogan cast his SCO push as a "360-degree" foreign policy rather than a break with the West.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, tracking companies listed on the emirate's exchange. It is the Gulf's principal listing venue for property developers and banks, and moved to a Monday–Friday trading week in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: Fighting between the US and Iran has moved onto the Emirates' own waters: US forces hit three Iranian oil tankers, and the UAE downed an Iranian drone offshore. Washington is also pressing the banking side, with Bessent targeting UAE banks over Iran ties, and Hormuz disruption has cut hotel demand to a fraction of normal.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The 30 largest companies listed on Bursa Malaysia in Kuala Lumpur, weighted by market value. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Prosecutors charged a third former prime minister, Ismail Sabri, with concealing $40 million in assets — the routine now of Malaysian leaders answering in court after leaving office. Days later the king consented to an emergency in Sarawak's Serian Division as smoke from Indonesian peat fires, burning on concessions held partly by Malaysian firms, pushed air quality into the hazardous band.

mkt:idx.standing: The main index of the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, tracking every listed company on the country's only bourse. Commodity producers and banks dominate it, in the world's largest Muslim-majority economy.
mkt:idx.recent: Prabowo's government opened 138 oil and gas exploration blocks to Russian bidders and pushed for early entry into force of a free trade agreement with the Eurasian bloc, with fertilizer and shipbuilding investment attached. Nickel smelters in Morowali keep running on captive coal, outside the accounting boundary that would price it.

mkt:tse.standing: The oldest and most-watched index of Japanese shares, a price-weighted average of 225 large companies listed in Tokyo. Asia's largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Treasury Secretary Bessent pressed the Bank of Japan to raise rates, and the yen then fell past 160 per dollar — a level that lifts the overseas earnings of Tokyo's exporters while raising the cost of the energy Japan imports. Fed hike odds moved to two-in-three as an oil shock reset the rate outlook.

mkt:hkex.standing: Hong Kong's benchmark index, tracking the largest companies listed in the city, most of them mainland Chinese groups. It is where Chinese firms meet foreign capital, so it doubles as the clearest daily read on outside sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: China's factory gauge rose to 51.5 in August, but the strength sat in AI capital spending rather than broad demand, and carbon emissions fell 1% on fuel substitution rather than slower output. Against that, a US trade group pressed Washington to ban Chinese vehicles outright.

mkt:sse.standing: The main board index of the Shanghai Stock Exchange, tracking every A-share and B-share listed there. Mainland China's principal market is largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Beijing has pushed state ambition into equities directly, framing humanoid robots as industrial strategy while banks, cafes and telcos hand out free AI inference as loyalty rewards. The factory gauge rose to 51.5 in August, though the AI capex boom that lifted it is narrowly concentrated. Washington is meanwhile rallying G20 partners behind tariffs on Chinese surplus, and a US trade group is seeking a ban on Chinese vehicles.

mkt:krx.standing: The main index of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, tracking every common stock listed on its senior board. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, which makes the index a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The Bank of Korea raised rates to 3.00% in a second consecutive increase, choosing financial stability over cheap money for leveraged exporters. SK Hynix said it was weighing closer ties with Kioxia, and Lee Hyoung-il was moved to finance minister in a reshuffle pairing that post with defence.

mkt:bse.standing: The 30-company benchmark of the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, Asia's oldest exchange, founded in 1875, and the index against which Indian equities are measured.
mkt:bse.recent: India's June-quarter output grew 7.8%, but the country slipped to sixth-largest economy because the league table converts nominal output into dollars and the rupee weakened. Economists questioned the figure itself: the growth arrived without new jobs or investment, and rests on a deflator that flatters real output.

mkt:sgx.standing: Singapore's benchmark index: the 30 largest companies listed on the Singapore Exchange, ranked by market value. Southeast Asia's financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.

mkt:twse.standing: Taiwan's benchmark index, the capitalisation-weighted average of every common share listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: Nvidia paid $3.5 billion for convertible bonds carrying a stake option in MediaTek, whose shares jumped 10% on the news and cemented it as an AI supplier rather than a handset chip designer. Taiwan also indicted nine people over AI server smuggling, an Nvidia manager among them.

mkt:set.standing: The main index of the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, covering the listed companies that meet its size and liquidity tests. Tourism flows and regional energy prices move it more than most markets in Asia.
mkt:set.recent: Thailand's push to move up the semiconductor chain runs through Washington: a handful of firms control the fabrication equipment any new plant would need, and export controls decide who gets it. That leaves the exchange's industrial names dependent on American licensing rather than domestic policy.

mkt:pse.standing: The main index of the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, tracking the 30 largest and most actively traded listed companies. A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: A Quezon City court ordered the arrest of Vice President Sara Duterte over alleged threats against President Marcos, setting bail at $1,900 per charge; she posted it and said she does not feel safe. The open rupture between the two families that share power in Manila is the sort of political risk a market this domestic prices directly.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Miners and energy stocks led the market lower into early September, and a Trump vow to "hit them hard" hit the index at the start of the month. The domestic backdrop hardened alongside it: home prices fell for a fifth straight month while rates stayed high, and KPMG Australia cut 27 partners and 360 staff.

mkt:jse.standing: The FTSE/JSE All Share Index tracks nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's national market. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the continent's only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The domestic news in this window is fiscal strain rather than corporate earnings: Gauteng's nurses gave the province a one-month ultimatum over health staffing, petrol rose R1.34 a litre despite a stronger rand, and Treasury moved on R88.6bn of unclaimed money sitting in dormant accounts and pensions. None of it accounts for the index, which is dominated by miners and rand-hedge listings earning offshore.

mkt:b3.standing: The main index of B3 in São Paulo, weighted by the most traded shares on Brazil's only stock exchange. Iron ore, oil and domestic interest rates drive most of what it does.
mkt:b3.recent: The collapse of Bank Master in a fraud investigation exposed a supervisory failure at the centre of Brazil's mid-sized banking tier, and a Sep 2 poll showing the president's lead evaporating turned the index into a bet on next year's fiscal settlement rather than on earnings.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones, the main index of the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City, tracking a weighted basket of the exchange's largest and most traded companies. It is tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.

mkt:byma.standing: Argentina's benchmark equity index, tracking the most heavily traded shares on the Buenos Aires exchange. Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years — direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: Milei reopened the Falklands sovereignty question, and Buenos Aires opened sanction proceedings against 45 companies and individuals drilling hydrocarbons off the islands without Argentine authorisation — a claim enforced through corporate liability rather than force. Trump then said the US position on the islands was under review, leaving the dispute's largest outside guarantor uncommitted.

mkt:tsx.standing: Canada's benchmark equity index, tracking the largest companies listed in Toronto by market value. Energy, mining and bank shares make up most of its weight, so it tends to move with commodity prices.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index climbed through a trade fight with Washington: Canada answered US tariffs with a 'dollar for dollar' list taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles, and Ontario Premier Doug Ford threatened to cut power exports south. Trump then demanded Canadian companies relocate to the US.

mkt:nyse.standing: The 500 largest US-listed companies weighted by market value, traded chiefly on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq. It is the benchmark most of the world's retirement savings are measured against, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: US forces struck three Iranian crude tankers, Iran said it hit six in reply, and a supertanker was stopped by mines in the Strait of Hormuz — the corridor most Gulf oil leaves through. Iran's security chief then vowed a "prohibited zone" near the strait, and about 50 US officers were ordered to take polygraphs over a leak about munitions stockpiles running down.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies by market value listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a weaker pound tends to lift the index.
mkt:lse.recent: Argentina reopened the Falklands dispute late in the window, with Milei threatening sanctions and then sanctioning 45 firms and individuals over UK-linked oil drilling, while a funding scandal put Nigel Farage's Reform under pressure. Neither reaches the overseas earnings the index rests on, and nothing else in the fortnight's reporting explains the move.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany's blue-chip index: the 40 largest companies listed in Frankfurt, weighted by tradable shares. Carmakers, chemicals and industrial engineering dominate it, so it reads as a gauge of foreign demand for German manufacturing.
mkt:xetra.recent: Volkswagen agreed a deal to cut 50,000 more jobs worldwide, the clearest signal yet that the carmakers at the index's core are shrinking to fit weaker demand. Against that, Germany named Russia over a bomb-rigged drone at Leipzig airport and found explosives on power lines in Saxony, putting industrial infrastructure itself in question.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest listed companies in France, traded on Euronext Paris. Luxury goods and energy dominate it, leaving the index unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Two French export lines drew state money in the window: Sweden ordered four frigates from Naval Group at €1.1 billion each, and the European Space Agency split €544 million between three rocket startups, passing over Ariane's own MaiaSpace on an award now only "expected to resume." Against that, France's maize harvest fell to a four-decade low.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange Index, the benchmark of Euronext Amsterdam and the world's oldest exchange. It tracks 25 Dutch blue chips, and one chip designer, ASML, carries so much of its weight that the index largely trades on semiconductor demand.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: Two Amsterdam-priced shocks framed the window. European gas topped €75 per megawatt-hour on the Dutch TTF benchmark that sets industrial power costs across the continent, with EU storage at a record low going into winter; days later the Dutch central bank moved $11.6bn of gold out of New York to London, a custody shift by the country's monetary authority.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main exchange. Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 most heavily traded companies on the Milan exchange, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, and it is the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Giorgia Meloni passed 1,413 days in office, making hers the longest-serving government in Italian history — a stretch of political continuity that has kept the sovereign spread the index trades against unusually quiet. Former leaders responded by pressing her to convert that stability into economic reform.

mkt:six.standing: The blue-chip index of Switzerland's main market in Zurich, tracking the 20 largest and most traded Swiss companies. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The 30 most traded companies on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms dominate it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: Stockholm signed a €4.3 billion deal for four French frigates from Naval Group, each costing €1.1 billion — an order that goes to a French yard rather than a Swedish one, and lands as four EU countries push to reopen the debate on using frozen Russian assets for Ukraine.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only public equity market. It trades Sunday to Thursday, and banks, defence contractors and technology firms carry most of its weight.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate untouched at the coming meeting. Traders price it against the two alternatives, a cut or a hike, so it reads as the market's bet on the Fed sitting still.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The hold bet lost ground as an oil shock and a payroll surge pushed traders toward a September hike instead: a Fed that had been expected to sit or ease is now being priced for tightening. Warsh said in Jackson Hole the Fed would have "work to do" if inflation did not fade.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The English-language Wikipedia entry for the 45th and 47th president of the United States. Daily readership on it rises and falls with what his administration is doing, which makes it a rough gauge of how far a decision has travelled.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The Sept 3 peak sat between two fights over what things are called: a federal judge in Baltimore enjoined a reissued birthright citizenship order, and the US Mint began selling a $1 coin bearing his face against a standing ban. He had also floated renaming the Strait of Hormuz and called the Iran war "small potatoes.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on the United States, a baseline-heavy page that most days reflects reference lookups rather than news, so movement in it marks moments when the country itself becomes the subject people go looking up.
wiki-united-states.recent: US forces struck Iran again after a month's pause, hitting new targets in a night of exchanges that killed 11, while a supertanker was stopped by mines in the Strait of Hormuz and the UAE intercepted a drone. CENTCOM later hit three Iranian oil tankers; Tehran said it struck six in reply, and Pentagon data put 794 US troops wounded.

wiki-nepal.standing: The daily count of people opening the English Wikipedia article on Nepal, a landlocked Himalayan state of about 30 million between India and China. It rises when the country reaches an audience that does not normally follow it.
wiki-nepal.recent: A glacial-lake outburst on August 26 — ice and rock collapsing rather than rain — sent a wall of water down the Trishuli valley in Rasuwa, killing more than 1,300 and leaving thousands missing, including 288 Indians and 41 Australians. Run-of-river hydropower is built into those narrow valleys for the gradient, which put 934 workers underground and downstream at once.

fed-funds.standing: The overnight rate the Federal Reserve sets for banks lending reserves to each other. It is the anchor for dollar borrowing costs everywhere, and mortgage, corporate and emerging-market debt pricing follows from it.
fed-funds.recent: Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole debut repriced the dollar, and markets swung from expecting easing to favoring a September hike. A payroll surge and an oil shock pushed hike odds to two-in-three, while the long end sold off on term premium rather than policy: the 10-year Treasury reached 4.81% and the 30-year mortgage rate 6.71%.

ecb-rate.standing: The rate the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on funds parked with it overnight, and the floor beneath every euro-area borrowing cost. Mortgages and business loans across the twenty countries reprice from it.
ecb-rate.recent: The easing cycle that took the rate down has run into a bond market moving the other way: long yields hit multi-decade highs on inflation fears, with the US 10-year at 4.81% and the 30-year mortgage rate at 6.71%. Central banks elsewhere have already turned — the Bank of Korea hiked to 3.00% and markets now favor a September Fed hike.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force that is out of work and actively looking, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is the figure the Federal Reserve weighs against inflation when setting interest rates.
us-unemployment.recent: A solid US jobs report on 5 September pushed Treasury yields and the dollar up and knocked equities back, the reaction of a market that reads a firm labour market as one less reason for the Federal Reserve to cut.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Nigeria, Africa's most populous country and its largest oil producer. Attention rises when politics, security or the economy there reach an international audience.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Uber shut its Nigerian and Ugandan operations with immediate effect, stranding drivers and passengers with no wind-down for contractors. Dangote Cement booked a London investor day rather than raise capital at home, and Moody's rewarded Abuja's austerity after foreign reserves reached a 20-year high.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the United States lifts its naval blockade of Iranian shipping by a set date. It is a bet on de-escalation, and it prices how likely traders think the maritime campaign is to be called off.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: The bet collapsed as the campaign widened rather than wound down: US forces struck three Iranian crude tankers, Iran said it hit six in reply, blasts sounded near the Kharg Island export terminal, and Tehran vowed to declare a prohibited zone near the Strait of Hormuz. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said there may be no nuclear agreement at all.

xag.standing: A silver-backed digital token traded on crypto exchanges, priced per troy ounce against physical bullion held in vaults. It tracks the metal used in solar cells, electrical contacts and industrial plating as much as it tracks investment demand.
xag.recent: The industrial side of silver demand kept expanding: China's solar capacity reached 1,286 gigawatts by July, overtaking coal, and Pakistan's regulator attached a battery-storage requirement to an 800MW solar and wind auction. Against that, the Dutch central bank moved $11.6bn in gold out of New York to London.

wiki-petroleum.standing: The Wikipedia article on petroleum — the crude liquid refined into fuels, plastics and fertiliser feedstock. Its readership rises when the price of oil becomes a political story rather than a market one.
wiki-petroleum.recent: The United States took majority control of PDVSA's fields, putting 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan reserves under contract through a vehicle called North American Blue Energy Partners, and María Corina Machado disputed the deal's legitimacy from Caracas. Strikes on Iran and tanker attacks then closed Hormuz, and US gasoline reached $4.03 a gallon.

poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Israel shuts its civilian airspace before the end of September. Airspace closures follow escalation that reaches Israeli territory, so the price is a bet on how far the regional fighting spreads.
poly-israel-closes-its-airspace-by-septe.recent: Netanyahu said during a Gaza visit that "we are not retreating," and the campaign widened north: Israeli strikes destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, killing seven, after ordering Arab Salim residents out that morning. Ben-Gvir set a first-year expulsion quota of 250,000.

wiki-flood.standing: The daily count of readers opening Wikipedia's article on floods, the general entry on water covering land that is normally dry. It fills up when a specific disaster sends people looking for the mechanism behind it.
wiki-flood.recent: A glacial-lake outburst — ice and rock collapsing, not rain — sent a wall of water down the Trishuli valley in Rasuwa, killing more than 1,300 and leaving thousands missing; crews pulled two people alive from a hydroelectric plant's tunnel after nine days underground. Nepal's China trade corridor closed again, and the WMO said El Niño is nearing record strength.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. It is priced by traders rather than pollsters, and it reprices within minutes of a court ruling, a candidacy filing or a coalition break.

us-cpi.standing: The year-over-year change in the US Consumer Price Index, published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It sets the reference rate for Social Security adjustments and wage bargaining, and the Federal Reserve's rate path answers to it.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: Daily count of tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz, the sea lane between Iran and Oman that carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil. There is no overland route around it, so any interruption reaches importers within days.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: The US struck three Iranian tankers and Iran said it hit six in reply, and a supertanker was stopped after striking mines in the strait. Three vessels turned back on a radio warning from the IRGC Navy without a shot fired, and Iran's security chief vowed a new prohibited zone; Energy Secretary Chris Wright said US Navy escorts are what keeps crude moving.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: The count of container ships passing daily through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, the 30-kilometre gate between Yemen and Djibouti that every Suez-bound box from Asia must cross. When it empties, cargo goes the long way around southern Africa.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Fighting has closed on the strait's own shoreline: Houthi forces advanced toward Mokha on the Yemeni side, killing 81 in a day, while Yemen's army fought for the hills above Taiz in a battle that has cost more than 120 lives since Thursday. A Houthi missile also struck a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu, extending the risk to the Red Sea's far end.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The count of ships passing through Egypt's Suez Canal each day, the sea link between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. Roughly a tenth of world trade moves through it, and vessels that skip it sail around Africa instead.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Traffic stays hostage to the war at the canal's southern approach: Houthi forces advanced on the Bab al-Mandab strait at Mokha, killing 81 in a day, and a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker at Yanbu. Cairo, meanwhile, hosted Xi Jinping and lost a major bank's access to the global financial system.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: The count of ships passing through the Panama Canal each day, the lock-and-lake shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. The locks run on fresh water from an artificial lake, so how many ships get through depends on how much it has rained.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: The canal's throughput is set by rainfall over its watershed, and the WMO said in Geneva that Pacific warming of more than 2C in six months has odds near 100% of persisting to February — the pattern that dries out Panama's catchment. Rosatom is meanwhile pitching the Northern Sea Route as an alternative at 100 million tonnes by 2032.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The daily count of ships passing through the Strait of Malacca between Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to East Asia. Most of the crude and containers bound for China, Japan and South Korea pass through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: Traffic through the strait carries the displacement from the fighting at the other end of the route. US strikes on Iranian crude tankers, a supertanker halted by mines in the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's declared plan for a prohibited zone have pushed war-risk premiums onto every eastbound cargo, while Houthi advances near the Red Sea strait close the alternative.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: A daily count of merchant ships passing through the waterway between Taiwan and mainland China, one of the busiest sea lanes in the world. Most of East Asia's exports and its imported energy move along it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The count of ships passing daily through the Strait of Dover, the narrow neck between England and France where the world's busiest shipping lane crosses the Channel ferry and freight routes linking Britain to the continent.
portwatch-dover-total.recent: Masked anti-migrant protesters shut Britain's busiest ferry port at Dover on 5 September, halting cross-Channel freight, and the local council leader said police were slow to respond. The UK government condemned the blockade, which cut the roll-on roll-off traffic that carries most goods trade between Britain and mainland Europe.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing daily through the Strait of Gibraltar, the nine-mile gate between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Everything sailing between northern Europe and Suez crosses it, so it registers reroutings decided far away.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The strait sits at the western end of the run that Hormuz and the Red Sea have made hazardous: a supertanker was stopped after hitting mines at Hormuz, the US struck Iranian crude tankers, and Houthi forces advanced on the Red Sea strait in fighting that killed 81 in a day. On its African shore, Morocco deported over 4,000 people from Tangier in 20 days amid the Ceuta crossings.

poly-will-marine-le-pen-win-the-2027-fre.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Marine Le Pen becomes president of France at the 2027 election. It prices what traders will pay on the leader of the National Rally, the party that has topped recent French national polling.
poly-will-marine-le-pen-win-the-2027-fre.recent: The window's political news ran with the European far right rather than against it: the AfD took a German state election, the first such win since the Second World War, and traders moved on that read-across rather than on anything from Paris. Nothing in the fortnight's French coverage accounts for the shift.

poly-will-josh-shapiro-win-the-2028-demo.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Josh Shapiro, the governor of Pennsylvania, becomes the Democratic Party's nominee for president in 2028. It is priced as a share of the whole field, so it moves as much on who else enters as on anything he does.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out on whether Benjamin Netanyahu holds the Israeli premiership after the next transfer of power. It is the cleanest running price on the durability of a coalition whose decisions on Gaza and Lebanon shape the region.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: Netanyahu told troops on a Gaza visit that Israel was "not retreating," and the campaign widened rather than wound down: strikes destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh and killed seven in southern Lebanon, while Ben-Gvir set a first-year expulsion quota of 250,000. Gaza's health ministry counts 1,334 dead since October's ceasefire.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Vladimir Putin ceases to hold the Russian presidency before the end of 2026, whether by death, resignation, removal or an unscheduled succession. It prices the perceived durability of a single leader.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: Nothing in the fortnight touched Putin's hold on office. The coverage was of the war and its edges — a Ukrainian strike on an oil depot near Sochi and sea drones reaching the city itself, Germany naming Russia over the Leipzig airport drone attack, and a battlefield halt Kyiv ordered for Sept. 5-8 to receive Witkoff and Kushner. None of it bears on the succession.

poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Chinese forces mount an invasion of Taiwan before the end of 2026. It is the cleanest live gauge of how much money is willing to back the tail risk that sits under semiconductor supply, Pacific shipping and US-China policy.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Marco Rubio becomes the Republican nominee for president in 2028. Prices are what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll, and they move on party signals long before any vote is cast.

poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-us-p.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if California's governor is elected US president in 2028. It is traded, not polled — the price is what buyers will pay for that outcome, and it moves years before any primary ballot exists.
poly-will-gavin-newsom-win-the-2028-us-p.recent: The venues carrying contracts like this one spent the window in court: the Ninth Circuit held that Kalshi's sports contracts are not "swaps", leaving them to state gambling regulators, and New Jersey has asked the Supreme Court to settle it. A White House aide who read speeches early was fined for betting on them.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Israel and Iran hold to a truce through a set date. It prices how much traders will stake on a pause in fighting surviving, and the same wager reprices with every strike and every mediated offer.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The window covered a US-Iran exchange rather than an Israeli one: American forces hit three Iranian oil tankers, Iran said it struck six in reply, and Tehran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone near the Strait of Hormuz. Energy Secretary Chris Wright then said there may be no nuclear agreement — the aim the campaign was declared to serve.

poly-will-openai-have-the-best-ai-model-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI's frontier model will be judged the strongest available at a set date, settled against a benchmark ranking. It is the closest thing to a traded price on which lab leads the field.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Clarity Act, a US bill numbered H.R.3633 that would set out which federal regulator governs digital-asset and event-contract markets, becomes law before the end of 2026. It pays out only on a signature.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: The legal ground shifted under the bill rather than in Congress. The Ninth Circuit held that sports-linked contracts are not "swaps," leaving states their gambling powers over Kalshi, Connecticut filed suit, and New Jersey has now asked the Supreme Court to settle the classification. A court answer arriving first makes a statute less necessary.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the party that has held a parliamentary majority since the 2000s, wins the most seats at the next State Duma election. It is one of the few tradeable markets on Russian domestic politics.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: Traders were pricing a party whose war is being pushed toward a negotiated end: Witkoff and Kushner were sent to Moscow and Kyiv with a plan to stop the fighting, and Ukraine ordered a battlefield halt for Sept. 5-8 to receive them. Against that, Germany formally blamed Russia for the Leipzig airport drone plot and the EU summoned its envoy.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-by-octob.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before a set date. Traders buy and sell the odds, so the price is what money says about the war ending, not a forecast anyone has issued.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-by-octob.recent: Ukraine ordered a battlefield halt from Sept. 5-8 for a visit by Witkoff and Kushner carrying a US plan to end the war, and the two armies stopped shooting around the Zaporizhzhia plant long enough for external power repairs. But the strikes kept widening: Ukrainian sea drones hit a vessel at Sochi and set an oil depot ablaze there, and Germany formally blamed Russia for a Leipzig airport drone attack.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if fighting between Russia and Ukraine stops under an agreed truce before the year is out. It prices what traders will stake on the war ending, not what any government has promised.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Kyiv ordered a battlefield halt for Sept. 5-8 to receive Witkoff and Kushner, and the two armies stopped shooting around Zaporizhzhia long enough for the IAEA to restore external power to the plant. Against that, Ukrainian sea drones hit a vessel at Sochi and set an oil depot ablaze there, and Germany formally blamed Russia for the Leipzig airport drone attack.

poly-israel-military-action-against-leba.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Israel takes military action in Lebanon by 29 September, priced as the share of a dollar traders will pay for that outcome. It is a bet on escalation, not a forecast of it.
poly-israel-military-action-against-leba.recent: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon killed seven and destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, with an evacuation warning issued for Arab Salim; Lebanon's health ministry counts 17 hospitals damaged since 2 March. Action already under way narrows what a contract on future action can still pay.

poly-will-1-fed-rate-cut-happen-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the Federal Reserve lowers its policy rate at least once during 2026. It is a live wager on US monetary policy, and it reprices whenever inflation or jobs data shifts what the Fed is likely to do.
poly-will-1-fed-rate-cut-happen-in-2026.recent: Traders moved the other way as an oil shock pushed the debate toward a hike rather than a cut, with hike odds reaching two-in-three, and a payroll surge that pressured gold hardened those bets further. Warsh said the Fed would have "work to do" if inflation does not fade.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The number of people reading the English Wikipedia article on Bitcoin each day. It rises when the cryptocurrency reaches beyond its own market — into mortgages, pensions, court filings and criminal cases — and is a rough gauge of how far outside that market the subject has travelled.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: The late-August peak followed a squeeze that carried the price to $80,020 rather than a wave of new leverage, with market makers running the basis trade taking the largest profits without a directional view. Better and Coinbase then launched a mortgage that lets the lender re-lend pledged coins, and six decade-old wallets moved $40 million.

poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-decem.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington and Tehran sign a nuclear agreement before the end of 2026. It prices what traders will pay for diplomacy rather than what analysts forecast, and it moves on statements from either capital.
poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-decem.recent: Energy Secretary Chris Wright said on the record that there may be no nuclear agreement — the objective the war was declared to serve — while strikes continued. US forces hit three Iranian oil tankers and Iran struck back at six; Iran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone near the Strait of Hormuz, and Pentagon data now counts 794 US troops wounded.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the United States lifts its naval interdiction of Iranian shipping before the end of 2026. It is a bet on the war's shipping dimension ending, not on a negotiated peace.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: US forces struck three Iranian crude tankers and Iran said it hit six in reply, while Iran's security chief vowed a prohibited zone near the Strait of Hormuz and Tehran stood up an economic war task force in its economy ministry. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said there may be no nuclear agreement — the deal that would have ended the interdiction.

poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Pete Buttigieg becomes the Democratic nominee for president in 2028. Traders buy and sell a share of the eventual payout, so its price tracks what money is willing to back rather than what pollsters find.
poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.recent: The venues carrying these contracts spent the window in court rather than in the campaign. The Ninth Circuit ruled in San Francisco that sports bets are not "swaps," leaving states their regulatory hand, and New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to settle the question; separately a White House aide paid a fine for trading ahead of speeches he had read. None of that explains this contract's price.

poly-will-base-launch-a-token-by-decembe.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Base, the Ethereum layer-2 network built by Coinbase, issues its own token before the end of 2026. Coinbase has repeatedly said it has no plans to, which is what keeps the price low.

stocks:DB.standing: Germany's largest bank, listed in Frankfurt and New York, with a corporate and investment banking arm that serves much of European industry. Its research desk's rate calls are widely read across the euro area.
stocks:DB.recent: The bank's research desk moved its European Central Bank peak forecast to 2.75%, adding a December hike on top of September and naming persistent energy risk as the reason. The concern is second-round transmission — a supply shock reaching wages and services pricing — which the ECB can only offset by suppressing the rest of the domestic economy.

poly-will-new-people-nl-gain-the-most-se.standing: A Polymarket contract that settles at 100 if the New People party wins the most seats in the election named, and at zero otherwise. The price is simply what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll or a forecast.

poly-will-nvidia-be-the-largest-company-.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if NVIDIA holds the top spot in global market capitalisation by a set date. It prices a bet on whether AI chip demand keeps one supplier above every other listed company on earth.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Kamala Harris becomes the Democratic nominee for president in 2028. Traders buy and sell shares in the outcome, so the price is what money is willing to pay for it, not a poll.
poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.recent: The fortnight's news about these markets was regulatory, not political: New Jersey asked the Supreme Court to settle whether event contracts are gambling for states to police or swaps for the federal CFTC, days after the Ninth Circuit ruled Kalshi's sports contracts were not swaps. Nothing in it bears on the nomination.

wiki-israel.standing: The Wikipedia article on Israel, and the number of people who open it each day. The count rises when the country is at the centre of a news event, so the line is a rough gauge of how far a story has travelled beyond the region.
wiki-israel.recent: Israeli strikes destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh al-Fawqa in southern Lebanon, killing seven. In Geneva, UN human rights chief Volker Turk told states to halt arms transfers to Israel where they risk being used in violations, and told companies to end business supporting illegal settlements. Gaza's health ministry says 1,334 have died since October's ceasefire.

stocks:WULF.standing: A US bitcoin-mining company that has converted its power-heavy sites into rented capacity for AI computing, so its shares trade on data-centre contracts and electricity costs rather than on the coin price alone.
stocks:WULF.recent: A fire at the Lake Mariner site drew firefighters who found three dead hydrants and no working alarm, exposing a gap in local oversight of the Somerset campus. Nothing else in the fortnight's reporting bears on the company's contracted capacity.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: Shares in Alphabet, the Mountain View holding company that owns Google — search, YouTube, Android, Maps and the Google Cloud business. Advertising sold against search results supplies most of its revenue, so the stock tracks the ad market.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: A federal judge in Alexandria ruled Google will not have to divest its ad exchange, leaving the auction business that sits between publishers and advertisers intact under a liability finding alone. In the same fortnight Google Maps began rendering one lake under two names depending on the country a user views it from, and MapQuest topped app charts by refusing the change.

stocks:NVO.standing: The Copenhagen drugmaker behind the semaglutide obesity and diabetes franchise, listed in New York as an ADR. One company's pipeline carries much of Denmark's export earnings and stock market value, so its trial results move a national economy.
stocks:NVO.recent: Novo Nordisk halted two cardiovascular outcome trials of ziltivekimab for futility. The drug tested the inflammation hypothesis of heart disease — that damping IL-6 signalling prevents heart attacks independently of cholesterol — and stopping for futility is a scientific verdict on that decades-old bet, not a strategic retreat.

stocks:066570.KS.standing: A South Korean consumer-electronics maker listed in Seoul, best known for televisions, home appliances and display panels, with a growing business selling advertising and viewer data through the TV sets it has already sold.
stocks:066570.KS.recent: Two reports in the window documented how far LG's advertising arm has pushed into the devices it ships: its automatic content recognition now tracks 363 million devices, keeps listening with the screen off, and scans the local network. The same technology has since reached computer monitors, closing the one display people bought to avoid it.

poly-will-company-c-be-the-largest-compa.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Apple holds the top spot in global market capitalisation by a set date. It prices the crowd's money on a ranking that turns on a handful of megacap valuations moving relative to each other.
poly-will-company-c-be-the-largest-compa.recent: The market these bets trade on spent the window under legal siege rather than reacting to Apple. The Ninth Circuit ruled in San Francisco that sports contracts are not "swaps," leaving states a hand in regulation; New Jersey then asked the Supreme Court to settle the question, and Connecticut filed against Kalshi.

stocks:TSM.standing: The world's largest contract chipmaker, listed in New York as an ADR. It fabricates the leading-edge processors that Apple, Nvidia and Qualcomm design but do not build, so its output constrains most of the industry's roadmap.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares in the Cupertino-based maker of the iPhone, Mac and Apple Watch, listed on Nasdaq. It is one of the most widely held stocks in the world, so index funds and pension portfolios move with it whether or not they chose it.
stocks:AAPL.recent: John Ternus took over as chief executive from Tim Cook on 1 September, inheriting a manufacturing base in Zhengzhou built to run without warehouses or inventory. Days earlier enterprise buyers cleared out Mac stock the company had not planned for, and OpenAI denied a claim that it took Apple trade secrets.

stocks:AMZN.standing: Shares in the Seattle retailer that runs the largest online store in the United States and, in AWS, the largest cloud computing business in the world. Retail supplies the volume; the cloud and advertising arms supply most of the profit.
stocks:AMZN.recent: The FTC and 22 states sued Amazon on 31 August over its advertising auctions, alleging advertisers were overcharged $20 billion through a surcharge and a clearing price they could not verify. A week later a Boeing 767 freighter in Amazon livery overran the runway at Miami International, crossed unpaved ground and struck a van and a car, killing five people on the ground.

stocks:BA.standing: The share price of Boeing, the American maker of commercial jetliners, defence systems and space hardware, and one of the two firms building nearly every large passenger aircraft in service.
stocks:BA.recent: The window's news carries one aviation story: the NTSB's account of a 767 freighter, flown for Amazon by a contract carrier, overrunning at Miami, in which at least 5 people died. Those findings were published after the price had already fallen, and nothing else in the period accounts for the move.
